articles.body: Iranian women have launched a campaign pledging their wedding rings as a symbolic reward for revenge against US President Donald Trump, with hundreds gathering in Tehran to express their support for retribution following recent wars.According to Iranian newspaper Tehran Times, the campaign, called ‘Rings of Revenge’, was launched by a group of women under the name ‘Madaraaneh’ (Maternal). The initiative was unveiled alongside a gathering titled ‘Rastakhiz of Tehran Women’, or ‘The Uprising of the Women of Tehran’, held on Thursday night, October 22, outside the main gate of the University of Tehran.Hundreds of women from different walks of life attended the gathering, including students, volunteers and the wives and daughters of those killed in the two recent wars. The programme featured speeches by women activists, choir performances and elegies, with revenge emerging as its central theme.The participants also joined the ‘Golden Retribution’ campaign, which encourages donations of gold and money to support what organisers describe as efforts to secure revenge. The Nehzat-e Madari movement, which runs the drive, has reportedly gifted gold donors bracelets bearing a bullet-shaped plaque as a reminder of their stated mission.Tehran Times reported that the organisers view retribution for the killing of Iran's former leader as a mission, with the donated jewellery serving as a symbol of their commitment.Since the war began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran has lost several key political, military and security figures, dealing a major blow to the country’s leadership. Among those killed were Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, national security chief Ali Larijani and senior commanders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).The campaign comes amid continuing tensions across the Middle East, with Iran's relations with the US and Israel remaining a major source of regional uncertainty. The wider conflict has also involved the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, who have continued to launch attacks against targets they describe as linked to their adversaries.Meanwhile, Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz on Monday denied reports of a rift between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the military leadership over a possible operation against Iran ahead of Israel's national elections. articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday that the government would announce concrete measures to address students' demands for better learning
articles.body: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday that the government would announce concrete measures to address students' demands for better learning conditions and more resources after weeks of protests, school blockades and demonstrations continue to fuel unrest across the country.Macron said Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu would announce “strong measures” after meeting student unions. However, he warned that further unrest remained a possibility, with more protests expected next Saturday.“I have also asked the government to respond to the legitimate demands that lie at the root of this social movement,” Macron told reporters during a visit to Marseille in southern France.The government is expected to announce changes to Parcoursup, France's national online university admissions platform, French media reported. Students have criticised its selection criteria, arguing that they lack transparency and limit equal access to their preferred courses.Their demands also include more teachers to cover staff absences, school renovations, changes to teaching hours and smaller classes. The government announced on October 8 that it would deploy 3,000 additional substitute teachers to high schools facing staffing shortages.The protests began with high school blockades in mid-September and have since spread nationwide. Students have accused the government of failing to address their concerns over poor school conditions and inadequate resources.Demonstrations on October 17 against rising living costs and poor school conditions turned violent, with groups setting fires, looting shops, storming public buildings and clashing with police. Protesters also briefly stormed Marseille City Hall during the unrest.A subsequent round of nationwide demonstrations on Saturday saw less violence. Authorities estimated that more than 400,000 people took part, while organisers put the turnout at nearly 800,000.The unrest has also led to mass arrests and renewed scrutiny of police crowd-control weapons, which have been blamed for causing life-changing injuries to some teenagers.The demands for better-funded schools, particularly in poorer communities, come as France faces record poverty and mounting public debt.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a major relief for local commuters, residents living within 20 km of a National Highway toll plaza can now opt for an annual concessional pass costing Rs 1,500 for plazas located outside municipal or local town limits and Rs 3,000 for those within such limits. Currently, eligible residents can obtain a monthly pass for Rs 360, amounting to Rs 4,320 annually.Road transport ministry notified the changes to NH Fee Rules on Monday. Under the provision, vehicle owners with valid and functional FASTags registered for personal use can choose either the existing monthly pass or the new concessional local pass for commuting through the specific toll plaza.Govt will revise these rates every year on April 1. As per the notification, the concession will be applicable only to the specific toll plaza and will not be transferable for use at other plazas. However, the pass will not be issued for NHs or expressways where toll is collected under a closed user fee collection system.The rules also make the concession conditional on the non-availability of a service road or alternative road for the vehicle owner or driver. articles.title: Wisconsin Rapids rejected a data centre plan for a former paper mill; the 1.2 million sq ft project now faces a year-long development freeze
articles.summary: Wisconsin Rapids, a city in the US state of Wisconsin, has rejected a proposal to transform a former paper mill site into a large data centre, ending
articles.body: Wisconsin Rapids, a city in the US state of Wisconsin, has rejected a proposal to transform a former paper mill site into a large data centre, ending months of debate over the future of the property. On October 20, 2026, the city's Common Council voted unanimously against the development permit, following concerns about the application and opposition from local residents. The decision comes as the city implements a year-long moratorium on new data centre developments, giving officials time to review local rules before considering similar projects in the future.Wisconsin Rapids declined the former paper mill data centre planAccording to WXPR's report, the Common Council voted 7-0 to reject the conditional use permit for the proposed hyperscale data centre. The project was planned for the site of the former paper mill, which had been a major part of the city's economy for more than a century.The decision followed an earlier recommendation from the city's Planning Commission, which voted unanimously against the application in September. Concerns centred on missing information and whether the developer had provided sufficient details to demonstrate that the proposal met the city's requirements.As reported by Civic Media, the commission identified gaps relating to electrical utility approvals, staffing plans, construction traffic and building layouts. The developer disputed the findings, maintaining that it had responded to the city's questions.The Common Council's final decision meant the application could not proceed under the proposed permit. It also reflected the wider debate about how the city should manage large technology developments and assess their potential effects on the surrounding community.What was planned for the former paper mill siteThe proposal was submitted by PNK Group USA, which sought to redevelop approximately 209 acres of the former mill property at 950 Fourth Avenue North. According to Civic Media, the planned campus would cover around 1.2 million square feet, combining the renovation of an existing building with the construction of four additional buildings.The development was intended to accommodate large-scale computing operations, including those associated with artificial intelligence. The proposed facility was expected to require approximately 150 megawatts of electricity, making power supply an important consideration in the planning process.The location was attractive to developers because of the infrastructure already available at the industrial property. Wisconsin Public Radio explained that the former mill had connections to electricity, roads, railways and other essential networks.However, the site's industrial history did not guarantee approval for a new development. The application still had to satisfy the city's planning requirements, while residents and officials sought greater clarity about the proposed facility and its potential long-term effects.The former paper mill became available for redevelopmentThe site has a long history in Wisconsin Rapids, where the paper industry shaped local employment and community identity. The mill opened in 1894 and became one of Wisconsin's largest paper-making operations.According to WPR, the facility specialised in glossy magazine paper during its later years. However, declining demand for that product contributed to its closure in 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic. The shutdown left nearly 1,000 people without jobs, marking a significant economic change for the city.Attempts to restart the mill or find a buyer were unsuccessful, and the industrial buildings were demolished in 2025. The cleared property subsequently became a potential site for redevelopment.WPR reported that a data centre proposal first emerged in December 2025. Interest in the site grew partly because of its existing electrical capabilities and its previous industrial use.Although the property offered an opportunity to attract new investment, its future became a source of disagreement. Some residents wanted a development that would create employment while addressing local priorities, rather than automatically accepting a large data centre as the next use for the land.Concerns raised by residents about the projectOpposition to the proposal developed over several months. According to WXPR, members of South Wood County Neighbors for Responsible Development organised against the development, attending meetings and working to prevent the project from moving forward.Residents raised concerns about noise and the potential effects of increased electricity demand on local energy costs. Questions also arose about the project's environmental implications and whether the information supplied by the developer was sufficient to assess its impact.The group formed in April 2026, and its campaign continued through public meetings and discussions with local officials. Marissa Johnson, a member of the organisation, told WXPR that opposing the proposal had become a sustained effort over the preceding 6 months.The developer also held meetings to explain the proposed facility and outline its potential benefits. Civic Media reported that PNK Group promoted the possibility of new jobs and investment, alongside a proposed $5.7 million community benefits plan.That plan included funding for public waterfront access, emergency response services, workforce training and river protection.How will the year-long development freeze affect future proposalsThe rejection of the permit comes alongside a separate decision to pause new data centre development. WXPR reported that Wisconsin Rapids introduced a one-year moratorium on October 9, 2026, with the option of extending it to 18 months.The restriction prevents new data centre proposals from proceeding while the moratorium remains in effect. City officials intend to use the period to review existing ordinances and determine whether additional rules are needed to assess future applications.Mayor Matt Zacher told WXPR that he was not opposed to all data centres but believed the city needed to take its time to ensure that developments were planned properly. He warned that a poorly designed facility could affect the community for decades.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: IISER Pune removes Umar Khalid's book from library ‘to avoid unrest’
articles.summary: IISER Pune withdraws Umar Khalid’s book “Fractured Communities” from its library after social media backlash, citing precaution to avoid unrest and unrest.
articles.body: Pune: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune has withdrawn ‘Fractured Communities’, a book based on the PhD thesis of jailed activist and former JNU researcher Umar Khalid, after its inclusion in the Srinivasa Ramanujan Library triggered a social media controversy over the weekend.The institute said the book was retracted “as a precaution in order to avoid any misunderstanding or unrest” after the matter was brought to the authorities’ attention. “The book collection at the institute library is built through recommendations from institute members, and a dedicated committee oversees the functioning of the library. On average, over 50 books from various areas are routinely added every month to the library,” the institute said in a statement.“Regarding the book in question, as soon as the matter was brought to the attention of institute authorities, it has been decided to retract the book as a precaution in order to avoid any misunderstanding or unrest. The institute will examine what further action or steps can be taken,” the statement read.The controversy began after a photograph of the book displayed on the library’s digital board under the title ‘New Additions of Books’ was shared on ‘X’ by the handle @GemsofAcademia on Saturday night. The post was widely shared, with Madabhushi Madan Gopal, chairperson of the institute’s board of governors, responding through his personal ‘X’ account.“As in-charge chairperson, BoG, IISER Pune, I am shocked to know this. This is retracted last night and action is initiated on those who played this mischief. I assure such things will not happen again in IISER Pune. Prof. Sunil Bhagwat, Director, has taken immediate steps. We need to be alert,” he wrote.In a subsequent post, Gopal said the institute had identified the person responsible for this and that prompt action had been initiated. “There should be suitable remedial measures,” he posted.Asked about the action referred to in Gopal’s posts, an IISER Pune official said the chairperson had tweeted in his personal capacity through his personal account.The controversy divided opinion online, with a section criticising a central science institute for recommending the book, while another defended it as a researched work on Adivasis.‘Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power’, released earlier this year, examines the history of Singhbhum’s tribal societies and is based on Khalid’s PhD thesis at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). Khalid has been lodged in Delhi’s Tihar Jail since 2020 as an undertrial prisoner in connection with a case registered under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and other provisions of law. articles.title: E100 flex-fuel vehicles get regulatory push ahead of launch
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Paving the way for roll out of flex fuel vehicles (FFVs) that can run on up to E100 — nearly 100% pure ethanol or about 93-95% ethanol-blended
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Paving the way for roll out of flex fuel vehicles (FFVs) that can run on up to E100 — nearly 100% pure ethanol or about 93-95% ethanol-blended with petrol — road transport ministry Monday modified changes in Central Motor Vehicles Rules.This comes barely months before some car manufacturers launch their E100 models.FFVs with an internal combustion engine can run on petrol, biofuels like ethanol or methanol, or any mixture of both stored in a single fuel tank. E100 fuels are “intended only for vehicles designed and certified to use it”.Officials said this is not applicable for other vehicles.“Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can’t use E85 or E100 fuel. Hence, the notification doesn’t require owners of existing vehicles to switch to these fuel categories or modify their vehicles now or in the future,” said a transport ministry official.TOI has learnt that the change in rules was essential for type approval and registration of FFVs on E100 considering that vehicle manufacturers are ready with their products.Depending on the vehicle’s design and certification, the range of blending may extend to E85 or E100, a fuel predominantly consisting of ethanol.Flex fuel technology is used in countries such as Brazil and the US.Ethanol has a lower fossil carbon footprint than conventional petrol and the use of higher ethanol blends can help reduce tailpipe emission of carbon monoxide (CO) and certain hydrocarbons. Greater ethanol use will also reduce dependence on import of crude oil.While govt notification will enable OEMs to manufacture FFVs, this won’t be enough to push adoption of these vehicles, experts said. This is evident as even after almost seven months of the launch of E85 cars, only 17 such vehicles have been registered.Industry players called reduction in GST on FFVs from 28% to 5% (on par with EVs) to bring down vehicle cost for buyers and compensate for mileage loss, which is about 27% while using E100 fuel.Besides, they sought a reduction in fuel cost to around Rs 75 a litre.But a bigger problem is availability of E100 given that there are only a handful of pumps, although it can run on other grades of ethanol-blended fuel.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Vivek Ramaswamy says his mother was defamed first by the Democrats. Who is Dr Geetha Ramaswamy?
articles.summary: In the wake of a major controversy over roping in the estranged mother of the rival candidate, Vivek Ramaswamy said on Monday that he did not start this
articles.body: In the wake of a major controversy over roping in the estranged mother of the rival candidate, Vivek Ramaswamy said on Monday that he did not start this fight. He is ending this after he found himself in it and it wad his mother who got defamed first by the Democrats, Ramaswamy said. “I’ll tell you the advice I was raised in: You never start a fight, but if you find yourself in one, you finish it, and you have to stand for what is right and what is true,” Ramaswamy said. “They’ve attacked me. They’ve defamed my mother to media silence. It’s unbelievable. And yet, at the same time, they’ll trot out anything to attack a Republican.”Who is Vivek Ramaswamy's mother? How was she defamed?Ramaswamy's rival Amy Acton issued a press release on August 12, calling Ramaswamy a 'billionaire scammer' who used his mother to manipulate clinical trials in "pump and dump" scheme. Ramaswamy's mother is Dr Geetha Ramaswamy who worked at Ramaswamy's pharma company. In 2014, Ramaswamy founded Axovant, a pharma company. The Democrats alleged that he used the company to "buy the rights to an inauspicious Alzheimer's drug" thar had repeatedly failed clinical trials. Ramaswamy was accused of hiring his mother who, Democrats said, "despite lacking relevant research experience, helped massage data from old clinical trials to make the drug appear more promising.""In 2015, touting his mother’s reinterpretation of the data to potential investors and regulators, Ramaswamy led Axovant to a $1.4 billion initial public offering, the largest in biotech history at the time. He spent the ensuing two years promoting the drug intepirdine as a possible breakthrough for the millions of Americans who have Alzheimer’s disease," Amy Acton's press release said."Ramaswamy used his mother’s dubious math to help raise $315 million during Axovant’s $1.4 billion IPO, figures the company reached on no revenue," it added.The allegation against Ramaswamy that he became an overnight billionaire when he was only 29 by a "pump and dump" scheme is old and he called it "debunked" as many reports established that there was no evidence that Ramaswamy knowingly ran a deliberate scam with the Alzheimer's drug. Her mother's role was questioned but there was no official complaint against them. During the campaign, Ramaswamy referred to the issue as "debunked".Ramaswamy's campaign, in an eye-for-an-eye move, got Dr Amy Acton's estranged mother to speak about her daughter. And Donna Arthur called her daughter a liar. “I love my daughter, but when I saw her lying about her opponent—and it's not easy for a mother to say this—but Amy has a serious problem,” Arthur said in the advertisement for which Ramaswamy's campaign spent $4 million.“She is a liar. She lies about her past. She says she grew up living in a tent. None of that is true. She's lied her entire life,” Arthur said.Amy Acton revealed her childhood trauma and how she was sexually abused by her stepfather, Cledith Arthur. Her mother did not side with her and eventually lost custody of Acton and her brother. The stepfather was charged with rape but he did not plead guilty and fled the state. He remained a fugitive until his death in 2004.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
